title: Live Streaming
summary: Live streaming is video on demand with no time to prepare. The broadcaster's stream must be received, encoded into several qualities, packaged, and spread across a CDN within a few seconds, continuously, for hours. Low-latency HLS keeps viewers two to five seconds behind real life by delivering tiny partial segments the moment they exist, while a separate chat system fans messages out to everyone watching.

walkthrough.title: Broadcaster goes live
walkthrough.text: OBS pushes the stream over RTMP or SRT to the nearest ingest point, authenticating with a secret stream key.

walkthrough.title: Ingest validates and forwards
walkthrough.text: The ingest edge checks the key and the stream's health (bitrate, keyframe interval), then forwards it over the provider's private backbone to a transcoding region.

walkthrough.title: Transcode in real time
walkthrough.text: GPU or ASIC encoders produce a ladder (1080p60 down to 160p) faster than real time, with aligned keyframes so players can switch quality cleanly.

walkthrough.title: Package as low-latency parts
walkthrough.text: The origin cuts each rendition into 2-second segments made of ~200 ms CMAF parts and publishes each part to the playlist the moment it is encoded.

walkthrough.title: Viewers pull from the CDN
walkthrough.text: Players request the playlist with a blocking reload: the CDN holds the request until the next part exists, then serves it. Thousands of viewers on one edge share a single origin fetch.

walkthrough.title: Chat in parallel
walkthrough.text: Chat travels over WebSockets with fan-out by channel. The broadcaster sees it too, so the delay between video and chat is what makes the stream feel interactive.

walkthrough.title: Record for replay
walkthrough.text: Segments are also written to object storage, so the stream is available as VOD as soon as it ends.

data.label: Broadcaster
responsibilities: Encodes camera and screen in real time on their own hardware.
Keeps a stable upload bitrate and a regular keyframe interval (e.g. 2 s).
Reacts to chat as part of the show.

failureModes.impact: Frames are dropped; every viewer sees stutter.
failureModes.mitigation: SRT with retransmission; encoder adapts bitrate; warn the streamer.

failureModes.impact: Someone else broadcasts on the channel.
failureModes.mitigation: Regenerable keys, one active session per key, alert on unusual IPs.

data.label: Ingest Edge

output.name: Forwarded
output.type: Validated stream to a transcode region

responsibilities: Accepts streams close to the broadcaster to minimise packet loss.
Authenticates stream keys and starts the session.
Moves the stream over a managed network rather than the public internet.

failureModes.mitigation: Broadcaster reconnects to another PoP; players hold a short buffer to ride it out.

failureModes.impact: Players cannot start or switch quality.
failureModes.mitigation: Validate on ingest and reject with a clear error to the broadcaster.

data.label: Real-time Transcoder
responsibilities: Encodes several renditions at least as fast as real time, continuously.
Aligns keyframes across renditions for clean switching.
Passes the source straight through for small channels to save cost.

failureModes.mitigation: Capacity headroom per job; drop the top rendition before falling behind.

failureModes.impact: Not enough encoders for new channels.
failureModes.mitigation: Pre-provision for scheduled events; source-only fallback.

data.label: Packager & Origin
responsibilities: Publishes each part as soon as it is encoded.
Answers blocking playlist requests the instant new parts appear.
Keeps a short rolling window of recent segments for live viewers.

failureModes.scenario: Origin overloaded by direct viewer traffic
failureModes.mitigation: Only CDN shields may fetch; request collapsing at the shield.

failureModes.impact: Playlist discontinuities cause player errors on failover.
failureModes.mitigation: Timestamps derived from the source; redundant packagers in sync.

data.label: Recording / VOD

input.name: Segments
input.type: All renditions as they are produced

output.name: Replay
output.type: Full broadcast + clips available after the stream

responsibilities: Archives every segment so the stream can be replayed.
Lets viewers make clips of moments during the stream.
Applies retention rules and copyright muting.

failureModes.impact: End of the stream missing from the replay.
failureModes.mitigation: Durable queue for segment uploads; finalise only when complete.
Audio fingerprinting on VOD and muting of flagged sections.

data.label: Live Chat

output.name: Fan-out
output.type: Message to every viewer in the channel

responsibilities: Delivers messages to hundreds of thousands of viewers in under a second.
Applies slow mode, spam filters, and moderator tools.
Keeps chat working even if video falters.

failureModes.mitigation: Sample or batch messages for huge rooms; hierarchical fan-out across edge servers.
Rate limits, follower-only mode, automated filters.

data.label: Viewers (Players)

input.name: Media
input.type: Parts and segments from the CDN

responsibilities: Plays a few seconds behind live, catching up gently by playing slightly faster.
Switches quality based on bandwidth.
Shows chat alongside the video.

failureModes.scenario: Tiny buffer on a poor network
failureModes.mitigation: Grow the target latency automatically for viewers with unstable connections.

failureModes.impact: Chat reacts to moments some viewers have not seen yet.
failureModes.mitigation: Playback-rate control towards a common target latency.

data.label: CDN Edges

output.name: Origin fetch
output.type: One fetch per part per edge

responsibilities: Holds blocking requests and serves new parts to all waiting viewers at once.
Collapses identical requests into a single origin fetch.
Scales to millions of concurrent viewers for big events.

failureModes.scenario: Edge does not support blocking reloads
failureModes.impact: Viewers poll; latency rises and origin load explodes.
failureModes.mitigation: Use LL-HLS-capable CDNs; fall back to standard HLS latency.
Multi-CDN with steering by real-time QoE.
